title: Asked Gemini about itself. Got a smartphone storage seminar.
context: Drew asked Gemini a question about Gemini. Gemini answered a question about everyone else.

exchanges.prompt: What's the longest video you could take?
exchanges.response: How long a video you can take depends entirely on the hardware, the software constraints, and whether you mean a standard smartphone, a digital camera, or an experimental setup. 1. Modern Smartphones (iPhones & Android): Smartphones do not have a hardcoded artificial timer, but continuous recording hits physical ceilings: Storage Capacity... Thermal Throttling & Battery... File System Limits... 2. Dedicated Video & Cinema Cameras: DSLRs and mirrorless cameras historically had a strict 29-minute, 59-second limit (originally created to avoid European import duty taxes on "video recorders")...

roast: The question had the word "you" in it. Gemini looked around the room like you were talking to someone behind it.
Cited HONOR four times to answer a question about Gemini. Sponsored by a phone it doesn't run on.
Explained EU import duties on camcorders before admitting whether it can watch a YouTube video.
Asked for a number. Got a FAT32 history lesson.
verdict: The only AI that answers "what can you do" with "well, what can a Sony FX3 do?"
